2027-05-25.title: Second Tuesday of the Apostles
2027-05-25.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: You have the words of eternal life
2027-05-25.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe). Pentecost opened the seven weeks of this season, which recalls the birth of the Church and the mission of the apostles. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and since Pentecost the Angelus (“The Angel of the Lord”) is prayed again in place of the Queen of Heaven. On Thursday our Church keeps the feast of the Body and Blood of Christ; today's Gospel closes the discourse on the Bread of Life.
2027-05-25.verse: Simon Peter answered him, “Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.”
theo: Paul's letter to Corinth takes an unusual turn. Some in the community are questioning his authority, and he answers with a burst of questions: “Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?” His credentials are not a diploma but an encounter and a community: he has seen the Risen Lord, and the Corinthians themselves are “the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.” In the Season of the Apostles this matters to us. An apostle is one who has been sent by the Risen Christ, and the proof of the sending is the life of the Church that grows from it. Our own Church in Kerala is the seal of the apostleship of Mar Thoma, and every parish, every family that prays, every child who is baptized, is still that seal. Paul then defends a right: those who preach the Gospel may live by it. A soldier does not pay his own expenses, the one who plants a vineyard eats its fruit, the shepherd drinks the milk of the flock; and the Law says, “You shall not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.” The Church has always taught that the faithful must help provide for the needs of the Church and of her ministers (CCC 2043).

Then comes the surprise. Having proved his right, Paul refuses to use it: “Nevertheless, we have not made use of this right, but we endure anything rather than put an obstacle in the way of the gospel of Christ.” He worked with his own hands as a tentmaker (Acts 18:3) so that no one could say he preached for money. Here is a principle for every Christian and every minister: what we are entitled to is not always what serves the Gospel. A priest may have a right to comfort, a parish committee to recognition, a parent to an apology, a worker to a holiday, and all may be just. But love sometimes lays a right aside so that Christ may be seen more clearly. The priests and religious who serve in our mission dioceses in North India, often in poverty and far from home, live this word of Paul every day. So do the parents who give up their own plans for a child with special needs. The question Paul puts to us is not ‘What am I owed?’ but ‘What might stand in the way of the Gospel, and can I remove it?’

The Gospel brings the long discourse on the Bread of Life to its crisis. Jesus has said, “Those who eat my flesh and drink my blood have eternal life” (John 6:54), and many disciples find it too hard. “Because of this many of his disciples turned back and no longer went about with him.” Jesus does not run after them to soften his words; he does not explain the Eucharist away as a mere symbol. Instead he turns to the Twelve: “Do you also wish to go away?” And Simon Peter answers for them all: “Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life. We have come to believe and know that you are the Holy One of God.” Peter does not say that he understands everything. He says that there is no one else to go to. That is often the faith of the Church in hard times: not a clever answer to every question, but a loyal heart that knows where life is found. The Catechism places this very scene at the heart of its teaching on the Eucharist: the Eucharist and the Cross are stumbling blocks, and the Lord's question echoes through the ages, inviting us to discover that only he has the words of eternal life (CCC 1336). The Gospel ends with a shadow: “Did I not choose you, the twelve? Yet one of you is a devil.” Even among the chosen, betrayal is possible. Two days before the feast of the Body and Blood of Christ, let us renew our faith in the Real Presence, and pray for those who have walked away, that they may hear again the question of Jesus and come back.
conn: Jeremiah could not stop speaking the word: “within me there is something like a burning fire shut up in my bones” (Jeremiah 20:9); Paul: “woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel!” (1 Corinthians 9:16).
The ox that treads the grain.
Deuteronomy 25:4, quoted again in 1 Timothy 5:18: “The laborer deserves to be paid.”
At Corinth Paul stayed and worked with Aquila and Priscilla, because they shared the same trade: they were tentmakers (Acts 18:3).
At Caesarea Philippi Peter says, “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God” (Matthew 16:16).
The psalmist: “Whom have I in heaven but you? And there is nothing on earth that I desire other than you” (Psalm 73:25).
Even an unclean spirit cried out, “I know who you are, the Holy One of God” (Mark 1:24); Peter confesses it in faith.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we stand where the Twelve stood: before the mystery of the Body and Blood of Christ that many found too hard. With Peter we say, Lord, to whom can we go? and receive the Bread of eternal life.
Paul laid aside his rights for the Gospel; at the altar Christ laid aside his glory and gave his very self. Every Communion invites us to give ourselves in the same way.
outline: A man who had every right, and gave it up.
Point 1 · Am I not an apostle?
The encounter with the Risen Lord and the seal of a living community.
Point 2 · No obstacle to the gospel
Point 3 · Lord, to whom can we go?
The hard saying, the departing crowd, and Peter's loyal faith.
A missionary sister from Kerala in a village of Madhya Pradesh, walking two hours to teach catechism, carrying nothing but a Bible and a water bottle.
“You have the words of eternal life.”
live: Give generously this month to your parish and to the missions of our Church.
Give up one thing you are entitled to this week for the sake of peace or the Gospel.
When a teaching of the Church is hard for you, say Peter's prayer: Lord, to whom can I go? and ask for light.
Make a visit to the Blessed Sacrament before the feast of the Body and Blood of Christ.
fathers: Peter answered for all, one for many, unity for the whole. Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life: as if to say, if we leave you, you who give us eternal life in your body and blood, where else shall we find it?

See how Paul, after proving his right, says he did not use it: he wants to show that he did more than the law required. He bore hunger and labour rather than give anyone a pretext to slander the Gospel.
magis: The first announcement of the Eucharist divided the disciples; the Eucharist and the Cross are stumbling blocks; the Lord's question, Will you also go away?, invites us to discover that only he has the words of eternal life.

In the most blessed sacrament of the Eucharist the body and blood, together with the soul and divinity, of our Lord Jesus Christ, and therefore the whole Christ, is truly, really and substantially contained.
The faithful have the duty of providing for the material needs of the Church, each according to his abilities.
Faith is a gift of God; we can lose it; to live, grow and persevere in faith we must nourish it with the word of God and beg the Lord to increase it.
saints: Second Tuesday of the Apostles. In the Latin calendar, St Bede the Venerable, priest and doctor; St Gregory VII, pope; St Mary Magdalene de' Pazzi, virgin (optional memorials).

23–29 May: second week of the Season of the Apostles. Sun 23: the Most Holy Trinity. Tue 25: in the Latin calendar, St Bede the Venerable, St Gregory VII and St Mary Magdalene de' Pazzi. Wed 26: in the Latin calendar, St Philip Neri. Thu 27: the feast of the Body and Blood of Christ, kept by our Church on the Thursday (the Latin Church in India keeps Corpus Christi on Sunday 30 May). Sat 29: in the Latin calendar, St Paul VI. Then Sun 30: Third Sunday of the Apostles; Mon 31: the Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
2027-05-25.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Holy One of God, you have the words of eternal life. When your teaching is hard and many turn away, keep us with you, and give us the loyal faith of Peter, who knew there was no one else to go to. Teach us, like your apostle Paul, to lay aside our rights rather than put an obstacle in the way of your Gospel, and to support generously those who proclaim it. Bless the missionaries of our Church who labour far from home. As we prepare for the feast of your Body and Blood, deepen our faith in your true presence, and bring back to your table all who have walked away. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever and ever. Amen.

catechism: Providing for the needs of the Church.
kidsaint: Bede was an English monk who lived more than twelve hundred years ago. He went to the monastery when he was seven and spent his whole life praying, singing the psalms, studying the Bible and writing books. He wrote the first history of the Church in England. On the day he died he was still translating the Gospel of John for his people. The Latin Church remembers him on 25 May.
2027-05-25.special: Second Tuesday of the Apostles. The Gospel closes the discourse on the Bread of Life, two days before the feast of the Body and Blood of Christ.
term: From the Greek for ‘one who is sent’. The Twelve, and Paul, were apostles because the Risen Christ sent them; the bishops are their successors. Our Church is called apostolic because it was founded on the witness of Mar Thoma and keeps the faith of the apostles.

family.explain: Jesus told the people that he would give them his own Body to eat and his Blood to drink. Many found this too hard and went away. Jesus asked his twelve apostles, ‘Do you also wish to go away?’ Peter said, ‘Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.’ At Holy Qurbana Jesus really gives us himself. Even when we do not understand everything, we stay with Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for people who have stopped coming to church, that they may come back to Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do this week to prepare for the feast of the Body and Blood of Jesus on Thursday?”

illus: A religious sister from Thrissur has worked for twenty years in a mission station in Madhya Pradesh. When she first arrived she had a salary of almost nothing, no vehicle and no electricity in the convent. Her family asked her to come home and teach in a good school in Kerala, where she could live in comfort. She wrote back: ‘I have every right to come home. But if I leave, who will teach these children to pray? Here I have learned what Paul meant: I would rather bear anything than be an obstacle to the Gospel.’ Today three of the children she taught are catechists in their own villages.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Holy One of God, you have the words of eternal life. We gather to listen to you; keep us faithful when your word is hard. Amen.
share: Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? (1 Corinthians 9:1). Where have I met the Risen Lord, and to whom does he send me?
We endure anything rather than put an obstacle in the way of the gospel of Christ (1 Corinthians 9:12). What right could I lay aside so that others may see Christ?
Do you also wish to go away? (John 6:67). When have I been tempted to walk away from Jesus?
Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life (John 6:68). How has Jesus kept me close in a hard time?
pm.resp: Lord, you have the words of eternal life.
interc: For the bishops, priests and missionaries of our Church, that they may proclaim the Gospel without obstacle.
For those who have walked away from the Church because a teaching was hard, that they may hear the Lord's question and return.
For a deeper faith in the true presence of Christ in the Holy Qurbana as we prepare for Thursday's feast.
For generous hearts in our parishes, to support the Church and the poor.
For ourselves, that we may never betray the Lord who chose us.
pm.close: Father, your Son gives us his Body and Blood, the bread of eternal life. Keep us faithful to him when his word is hard, and make us generous servants of his Gospel. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, in today's reading Paul asks, “Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord?” He has met the Risen Lord, and the Church at Corinth is the proof of his mission.
Paul shows that those who preach the Gospel have a right to be supported, as a soldier, a farmer or a shepherd lives by his work. The Church still asks us to support her ministers and her mission.

But then Paul says that he gave up this right: “we endure anything rather than put an obstacle in the way of the gospel of Christ.” He worked with his own hands so that no one could say he preached for money.

In the Gospel Jesus has spoken about eating his Body and drinking his Blood. Many disciples find this too hard and leave. Jesus does not change his words. He asks the Twelve, “Do you also wish to go away?”
Peter answers, “Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.” Peter does not understand everything, but he knows that life is found only in Jesus.
On Thursday we celebrate the feast of the Body and Blood of Christ. Let us renew our faith that Jesus is truly present in the Holy Qurbana, and let us say with Peter: Lord, to whom can we go? Amen.
kids: Children, once Jesus said something very hard to understand, and many people walked away. Jesus asked his friends, ‘Will you go away too?’ Peter said, ‘Lord, where would we go? Only you give us eternal life!’
When something is hard, stay close to Jesus like Peter. On Thursday we celebrate Jesus in the Holy Qurbana. Say thank you to him!

intro: Theme: “Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.”
Paul's apostleship sealed by a living Church, his rights laid aside so that nothing may block the Gospel, and Peter's loyal faith when many walk away from the Bread of Life.

sub: An encounter with the Risen Lord.
Woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel.
q: If I say, “I will not mention him, or speak any more in his name,” then within me there is something like a burning fire shut up in my bones; I am weary with holding it in, and I cannot.
If I proclaim the gospel, this gives me no ground for boasting, for an obligation is laid on me, and woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel!
points.apply: Speak of your faith this week to one person who does not know Christ well.

If others share this rightful claim on you, do not we still more? Nevertheless, we have not made use of this right, but we endure anything rather than put an obstacle in the way of the gospel of Christ.

concl: The apostles were sent by the Risen Lord and gave up their rights so that the Gospel might run unhindered; Peter stayed when many left, because only Jesus has the words of eternal life.
Let us stay with him, support his mission and prepare our hearts for the feast of his Body and Blood.
2027-05-25.resolve: This week, speak of Christ to one person, give generously to the missions, and make a visit to the Blessed Sacrament before Thursday.
